falsifiable_prediction: Across-question fixation shift (distributional distance) is under 25% of across-image shift, and fixation-saliency correlation exceeds fixation-relevance correlation. KILL: the claim dies if across-question shift reaches 60% of across-image shift (looking is genuinely question-driven).
why_important: Question-conditioned looking is the core premise of active perception loops; measuring its actual strength tells the field whether to fix the conditioning mechanism or stop claiming it.
why_possibly_novel: MODEL SPECULATION (unverified): human question-conditioned gaze is documented in vision science; the corresponding causal measurement for agent loops may not exist.
minimal_falsification_experiment: For public images with multiple questions and annotated evidence regions, log agent crop choices per question; compute across-question vs across-image distributional shifts and correlations with saliency maps vs evidence regions.
main_risk: Some benchmarks' questions all target the same salient object, deflating across-question shift for reasons other than policy weakness; needs region-diverse question sets.
community_default_belief: Where the agent looks is driven by what it is asked — that is what makes it an agent rather than a preprocessor.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Crop proposals plausibly come from generic objectness signals in the encoder, with the question applied only at the answering stage — guidance in name only.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Half a day, single GPU: 100 images x 3 questions with evidence annotations, shift and correlation statistics. Public data only.

evidence_label.falsifiable_prediction: EXPECTED RESULT (pre-registered threshold; no measured numbers)
evidence_label.prior_work_basis: VERIFIED PRIOR WORK (well-known): question-conditioned human gaze studies exist in vision science; the agent-loop measurement is MODEL SPECULATION.

one_line_idea: A single forced confirmatory zoom on the claimed evidence region after answering cuts hallucinated-detail errors at negligible cost, because most hallucinations are never re-inspected by the loop.
problem: Agents assert visual details (text content, small attributes, presence claims) without any step that goes back to look at the pixels the claim is about; hallucinations survive because nothing in the loop ever confronts them with their referent.
core_hypothesis: A minimal protocol change — after drafting an answer, the agent must localize its evidence region, zoom into it, and re-affirm or retract — removes the subset of hallucinations that direct re-inspection can falsify, at the cost of one crop encode per answer.
falsifiable_prediction: Confirmatory fixation cuts hallucinated-detail error by at least 25% relative with under 10% compute overhead, and retractions are concentrated on genuinely wrong claims (precision of retraction above 0.7). KILL: the claim dies if the reduction is under 8% or retractions are indiscriminate.
why_important: It is the cheapest possible grounding mechanism — one extra look — and if it works it belongs in every deployed multimodal assistant as a default safety layer.
why_possibly_novel: MODEL SPECULATION (unverified): verification and zooming exist separately; mandatory post-answer evidence fixation as a hallucination-specific protocol with retraction-precision accounting may be new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: On hallucination-prone public benchmarks, run base vs confirmatory-fixation protocols with one open VLM; type errors as hallucinated-detail vs other; measure the reduction, overhead, and retraction precision.
main_risk: The agent may zoom into a wrong region that appears to confirm its claim, or retract true claims about regions it localizes poorly.
community_default_belief: Hallucination is a model-level pathology to be fixed with training interventions, not with loop protocol.
why_it_might_be_wrong: A claim never compared against its referent can survive regardless of model quality; the loop, not the weights, decides whether that comparison ever happens.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Half a day, single GPU: 300 instances, both protocols, typed-error comparison. Public data only.

evidence_label.community_default_belief: MODEL SPECULATION (inferred from training-centric hallucination work)
evidence_label.falsifiable_prediction: EXPECTED RESULT (pre-registered threshold; no measured numbers)
evidence_label.prior_work_basis: MODEL SPECULATION: no verified prior mandatory post-answer fixation protocol.

one_line_idea: Loop step order is a first-class variable: agents that draft an answer before zooming anchor on the draft and ignore contradicting crop evidence, while zoom-first ordering avoids the anchor at identical compute.
problem: Frameworks freely interleave drafting and evidence gathering, implicitly assuming the final synthesis weighs all context equally regardless of when it arrived; anchoring research on humans says order matters, and nothing has checked the agent analog.
core_hypothesis: A drafted answer in the transcript acts as an anchor: when subsequent crops contradict it, the agent disproportionately retains the draft; reversing the order (gather crops, then draft) removes the anchor and changes final answers on exactly the contradicted subset.
falsifiable_prediction: Answer-first agents retain contradicted draft answers at least twice as often as zoom-first agents produce those answers, at identical compute and crop content. KILL: the claim dies if the retention ratio is 1.2 or below (no meaningful anchoring).
why_important: Step ordering is free to change; if it causally moves accuracy on contradicted cases, every framework's default interleaving deserves an audit, and 'draft early' turns out to be an anti-pattern.
why_possibly_novel: MODEL SPECULATION (unverified): anchoring is documented in human judgment and in some text-model settings; a controlled order-manipulation with contradiction-conditioned accounting in visual loops may be new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Construct instances where full-resolution crops contradict the low-resolution first impression; run both orderings with matched content; measure retention of the contradicted answer conditioned on the crop evidence being decisive.
main_risk: Constructing genuinely decisive contradiction cases requires care; ambiguous crops would dilute both arms symmetrically.
community_default_belief: The final answer synthesizes all evidence in context; whether a draft came before or after a crop is immaterial.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Autoregressive agents re-read their own committed text as evidence; a stated draft is not a scratchpad note but a prior the model defends.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Half a day, single GPU: 200 contradiction instances, both orderings, retention ratio. Public data only.

evidence_label.community_default_belief: MODEL SPECULATION (inferred from framework interleaving freedom)
evidence_label.falsifiable_prediction: EXPECTED RESULT (pre-registered threshold; no measured numbers)
evidence_label.prior_work_basis: VERIFIED PRIOR WORK (well-known): human anchoring is documented; the loop-order causal claim is MODEL SPECULATION.

one_line_idea: Agents cannot judge evidence sufficiency — prompted 'can you answer now?' probes are near chance — but a small stopping head trained on loop traces predicts sufficiency well, converting wasted fixed-depth loops into adaptive ones.
problem: Active-viewing loops run to fixed depth because there is no reliable stop signal: the agent's own verbal judgment of whether it has seen enough is untested, and if it is unreliable, every loop over- or under-spends per instance.
core_hypothesis: Sufficiency information exists in the loop's state (answer stability across recent steps, crop-content statistics) even though verbal self-probes cannot express it; a lightweight trained head on those features predicts whether further looking will change the answer, enabling adaptive stopping.
falsifiable_prediction: The prompted self-probe achieves at most 0.6 AUC at predicting whether more crops change the answer, while the trained stopping head reaches at least 0.75 AUC and cuts average loop depth by 30% at equal accuracy. KILL: the claim dies if the prompt probe reaches 0.7 (no head needed) or the head stays at or below 0.65.
why_important: Adaptive stopping is the difference between loops that are deployable at scale and loops that are demos; a validated stop signal cuts cost on the easy majority without sacrificing the hard tail.
why_possibly_novel: MODEL SPECULATION (unverified): learned halting exists inside architectures (adaptive computation time); trace-trained stopping heads for LLM-orchestrated visual loops may be new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Run fixed-depth loops on public benchmarks logging per-step answers and features; define sufficiency ground truth as answer-stability-to-end; evaluate the verbal probe vs the trained head on held-out instances; then deploy the head as a stopper and measure the cost-accuracy tradeoff.
main_risk: The head may exploit benchmark-specific difficulty correlates and fail to transfer across task families.
community_default_belief: If the agent needs to stop, ask it — strong LLMs can introspect on whether they have enough information.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Verbalized introspection and actual state are weakly coupled in current models; the state knows things the mouth cannot say.
fastest_falsification_experiment: One day, single GPU: 500 logged episodes, probe-vs-head AUC comparison. Public data only.

evidence_label.falsifiable_prediction: EXPECTED RESULT (pre-registered threshold; no measured numbers)
evidence_label.prior_work_basis: VERIFIED PRIOR WORK (well-known): adaptive computation time exists inside networks; loop-level trained stopping is MODEL SPECULATION.

family_fingerprint.manipulated_variable: stop-signal source (verbal probe vs trained head)

one_line_idea: Accuracy versus number of accumulated crops is non-monotone: beyond a small working set, added crops interfere with earlier evidence and net accuracy declines, giving each controller a measurable optimal working-set size.
problem: Active-viewing loops accumulate crops into context on the assumption that more evidence monotonically helps, but multi-image interference in current VLMs suggests a capacity limit the loop should respect and currently ignores.
core_hypothesis: There is an interior optimum in working-set size: relevant crops added beyond it displace or interfere with the use of earlier crops, so accuracy rises, peaks, and falls — and the peak location is a stable property of the controller measurable once and reusable as a loop parameter.
falsifiable_prediction: With relevance held fixed by construction, accuracy peaks at 8 or fewer crops and declines by at least 3 points by 24 crops. KILL: the claim dies if accuracy is monotone non-decreasing in crop count up to 24.
why_important: A known working-set limit converts loop design from 'gather everything' to windowed evidence management (summarize-and-evict), and predicts which tasks need memory architectures rather than bigger contexts.
why_possibly_novel: MODEL SPECULATION (unverified): multi-image degradation is reported anecdotally for VLMs; a controlled working-set curve with relevance held constant, framed as a loop design parameter, may be new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Construct tasks where k relevant crops are available and answer difficulty is constant in k by design; sweep k for two open controllers; locate peaks and test peak stability across task families.
main_risk: Holding difficulty constant while varying k is delicate; leakage of difficulty into k would fake the decline.
community_default_belief: More relevant evidence in context cannot hurt; context limits are about length, not interference.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Visual tokens compete: each added crop dilutes attention over the others, and past the model's binding capacity the marginal crop costs more than it adds.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Half a day, single GPU: k-sweep at 4 values on 200 constructed instances. Public data only.

evidence_label.falsifiable_prediction: EXPECTED RESULT (pre-registered threshold; no measured numbers)
evidence_label.prior_work_basis: MODEL SPECULATION: anecdotal multi-image degradation reports exist; the controlled working-set law is unverified.

family_fingerprint.manipulated_variable: accumulated crop count at fixed relevance

one_line_idea: Enumeration loops that mark counted instances repair the systematic undercount of one-shot VLM counting on dense scenes: the fix is loop structure, not model scale, and the crossover density is measurable.
problem: VLMs undercount dense scenes in a single pass, and the default remedy is bigger models; but counting is algorithmically a loop (find, mark, repeat), suggesting the deficit is architectural mismatch rather than capability shortfall.
core_hypothesis: Externalizing the counting algorithm — the loop marks each counted instance on the image and re-queries for unmarked ones until none remain — removes the working-memory bottleneck that causes undercounting, with gains growing in scene density while model scale at fixed protocol gains little.
falsifiable_prediction: Marking-enumeration cuts absolute counting error by at least 40% relative on scenes above roughly 20 instances, while a one-class model upgrade under one-shot protocol cuts it by less than half that. KILL: the claim dies if enumeration helps under 15% or the bigger one-shot model matches it.
why_important: It cleanly demonstrates a loop-borne capability — an algorithm wrapped around a percept — and counting is a deployable primitive (inventory, biology, crowd safety) where systematic undercount is a known practical failure.
why_possibly_novel: MODEL SPECULATION (unverified): mark-based prompting and counting benchmarks exist separately; the enumeration-loop-with-visual-state protocol and its density crossover may be new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Implement the mark-and-requery loop over one open VLM; evaluate against one-shot counting on public counting benchmarks stratified by instance density; add the model-scale control at fixed protocol.
main_risk: Mark occlusion alters the scene as counting proceeds, potentially hiding uncounted instances behind marks in extreme density.
community_default_belief: Counting improves with model scale and better training data; it is a perception capability, not a protocol question.
why_it_might_be_wrong: No fixed-pass system can count unboundedly many things; humans externalize counting state too, and the loop can give the model the same tool.
fastest_falsification_experiment: One day, single GPU: enumeration vs one-shot on 300 density-stratified scenes. Public data only. Counting error metric, no segmentation masks involved.

evidence_label.community_default_belief: MODEL SPECULATION (inferred from scale-centric counting work)
evidence_label.falsifiable_prediction: EXPECTED RESULT (pre-registered threshold; no measured numbers)
evidence_label.prior_work_basis: VERIFIED PRIOR WORK (well-known): mark-based prompting and counting benchmarks exist; the stateful enumeration protocol claim is MODEL SPECULATION.

one_line_idea: In multi-view settings, language-reasoned next-view selection adds little over random next views except on the occlusion-limited subset — and that subset is identifiable in advance, telling systems when view planning is worth its cost.
problem: Next-view selection by LLM reasoning is an appealing story, but its marginal value is bounded by how often the answer is actually blocked from the current view — a base rate no one measures before building the planner.
core_hypothesis: View-planning value is concentrated: on most multi-view instances any additional view suffices (or none is needed), so reasoned selection matches random; only where occlusion geometry makes most views uninformative does reasoning pay, and a cheap occlusion probe identifies that subset beforehand.
falsifiable_prediction: Reasoned view selection beats random next views by under 2 points overall but by at least 5 points on the occlusion-limited subset flagged by the probe. KILL: the claim dies if reasoned selection wins by 5+ points overall (planning is broadly valuable) or fails to win on the flagged subset.
why_important: It scopes an expensive mechanism to the cases that justify it, and offers a template for auditing agentic components: measure the base rate of the problem the component claims to solve.
why_possibly_novel: MODEL SPECULATION (unverified): next-best-view is classical in robotics with geometric methods; base-rate-scoped evaluation of LLM view reasoning on public multi-view data may be new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Use public multi-view object datasets; define question sets with known per-view answerability; compare reasoned vs random next-view policies overall and on the probe-flagged occlusion subset.
main_risk: Multi-view benchmarks may under-represent hard occlusion, making the flagged subset too small for significance.
community_default_belief: Choosing the next view intelligently is obviously better than choosing at random; the only question is how much better.
why_it_might_be_wrong: When most views answer the question, selection cannot matter; component value is bounded by problem prevalence, not by component sophistication.
fastest_falsification_experiment: One day, single GPU: 200 multi-view instances, both policies, subset analysis. Public data only.

evidence_label.falsifiable_prediction: EXPECTED RESULT (pre-registered threshold; no measured numbers)
evidence_label.prior_work_basis: VERIFIED PRIOR WORK (well-known): next-best-view is classical in robotics; the base-rate-scoped LLM evaluation is MODEL SPECULATION.

one_line_idea: End-answer variance in active-viewing agents decomposes cleanly into controller-sampling, crop-selection, and tool-noise components — and controller sampling dominates, meaning reproducibility fixes should start at the controller, not the vision stack.
problem: Agent pipelines are irreproducible run to run, but nobody knows which stage's randomness matters, so stabilization effort (seeding tools, caching crops, freezing prompts) is spent blindly.
core_hypothesis: A nested-seeding design (fix all stages, release one at a time) yields a stable variance decomposition; the controller's token sampling contributes the majority of end-answer variance, with crop selection second and vision-tool nondeterminism a distant third — a mechanism-level result that prioritizes stabilization work.
falsifiable_prediction: The controller-sampling component accounts for at least 50% of end-answer variance across tasks, and freezing it alone cuts run-to-run disagreement by at least 40%. KILL: the claim dies if the controller share is under 25% (variance lives elsewhere).
why_important: Reproducibility of agent systems is a prerequisite for both science and deployment; knowing the dominant randomness source converts a vague problem into a targeted fix.
why_possibly_novel: MODEL SPECULATION (unverified): variance decomposition is standard statistics; applying nested-seed ANOVA to attribute agent-pipeline randomness across stages may be new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Implement nested seeding in an open active-viewing pipeline; run the release-one-stage design over public benchmarks with 10 replicates per cell; fit the variance decomposition and validate the freeze-the-top-component prediction.
main_risk: Stage interactions (crop choice depends on controller samples) complicate clean attribution; the design must account for the causal ordering.
community_default_belief: Agent nondeterminism is a diffuse property of having many components; you fix it by seeding everything or accepting it.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Diffuse-blame intuitions usually hide a dominant term; pipelines are chains, and one stage's entropy typically swamps the rest.
fastest_falsification_experiment: One day, single GPU: 100 instances, 3-stage nested seeding, 5 replicates, decomposition estimate. Public data only.

evidence_label.falsifiable_prediction: EXPECTED RESULT (pre-registered threshold; no measured numbers)
evidence_label.prior_work_basis: VERIFIED PRIOR WORK (well-known): nested ANOVA is standard; its application to agent-loop stage attribution is MODEL SPECULATION.

one_line_idea: Maintaining a persistent low-resolution global view alongside high-resolution foveal crops beats sequences of uniform crops at equal token budget, because zoom loops measurably lose global context — scale and off-crop relations — when the overview is dropped.
problem: Zoom loops replace the full image with crops to spend tokens on resolution, silently discarding the overview; errors about scale, position, and relations to off-crop content follow, but the tradeoff has never been isolated as a design variable.
core_hypothesis: The failure is architectural, not perceptual: a foveal layout (persistent downscaled overview plus current crop, same total tokens as two crops) preserves the global reference frame, cutting scale and relation errors relative to crops-only loops without any model change — the visual analog of keeping the map while reading the street sign.
falsifiable_prediction: The global+foveal layout beats crops-only by at least 4 points on scale/relation questions at matched token budget, with no loss on detail questions. KILL: the claim dies if the gain is 1 point or less or detail accuracy drops by 2+ points.
why_important: It defines a loop-level design principle (never drop the overview) that is free to adopt, and provides the measurement isolating which errors are caused by the loop's evidence layout rather than the model.
why_possibly_novel: MODEL SPECULATION (unverified): multi-resolution processing is standard inside architectures; enforcing a foveal layout at the loop's evidence-management level, with error-type attribution, may be new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Build both layouts over one open VLM at matched token budgets; evaluate on question sets typed as detail vs scale/relation over public images; attribute error changes to question type.
main_risk: The downscaled overview consumes budget that pure-detail tasks would rather spend on a second crop, so the layout may need question-type gating.
community_default_belief: Zooming is the fix for resolution limits; what the crop excludes is no longer relevant once the region of interest is found.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Many questions are relational or scale-dependent, and a crop erases exactly the reference frame those questions need; the loop should manage evidence like a fovea, not like a slideshow.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Half a day, single GPU: 300 typed questions, both layouts, per-type accuracy. Public data only.

evidence_label.community_default_belief: MODEL SPECULATION (inferred from crop-replacement zoom designs)
evidence_label.falsifiable_prediction: EXPECTED RESULT (pre-registered threshold; no measured numbers)
evidence_label.prior_work_basis: MODEL SPECULATION: multi-resolution architectures exist internally; loop-level foveal evidence layout unverified.

one_line_idea: Multi-agent visual debate converges to the shared percept, not the truth: same-backbone debaters agree more and stay wrong on perception errors, with stated confidence rising while accuracy is flat.
problem: Debate protocols are imported from reasoning tasks into multimodal settings assuming argument quality filters truth, but when all debaters share the same misperception, argumentation has nothing true to converge on.
core_hypothesis: Debate's value is bounded by percept decorrelation: same-backbone debates on perception-bound errors produce consensus without correction (confidence up, accuracy flat), while mixed-backbone debates recover a real fraction of those errors — making encoder diversity, not debate structure, the active ingredient.
falsifiable_prediction: Same-backbone debate gains at most 1 point over a single agent on perception-bound splits while stated confidence increases; mixed-backbone debate gains at least 3 points on the same splits. KILL: the claim dies if same-backbone debate gains 4+ points on perception-bound errors.
why_important: Debate is being packaged as a general reliability mechanism; knowing it is inert without percept diversity redirects engineering toward heterogeneous ensembles and prevents false safety claims.
why_possibly_novel: MODEL SPECULATION (unverified): multiagent-debate papers exist for reasoning tasks; a perception-stratified decomposition with backbone-diversity controls and confidence tracking may be new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Run 3-round debates on perception-bound and reasoning-bound splits with same-backbone and mixed-backbone agent pairs from open VLMs; log accuracy, agreement, and stated confidence per round.
main_risk: Confidence statements are prompt-sensitive; confidence tracking needs a fixed elicitation protocol to be comparable across rounds.
community_default_belief: Agents debating each other catch each other's mistakes; more debate means more error correction.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Debaters can only argue from what they see; identical eyes make debate an echo chamber with better rhetoric.
fastest_falsification_experiment: One day, single GPU: 300 stratified instances, both pairings, round-wise curves. Public data only.

evidence_label.falsifiable_prediction: EXPECTED RESULT (pre-registered threshold; no measured numbers)
evidence_label.prior_work_basis: VERIFIED PRIOR WORK (well-known): multiagent debate protocols exist; the percept-decorrelation bound is MODEL SPECULATION.

one_line_idea: Vision-agent ensemble gains come from vision-encoder diversity, not LLM diversity: mixing LLMs over a shared encoder yields little, while mixing encoders under one LLM captures most of the full-ensemble gain.
problem: Multi-agent vision systems diversify at the agent level (different models, prompts, temperatures) without knowing which axis of diversity actually decorrelates errors on visual tasks.
core_hypothesis: Visual errors originate mostly in the encoder, so ensemble decorrelation requires encoder diversity: a 2x2 factorial (encoder same/different x LLM same/different) will show the encoder factor dominating ensemble gain, with LLM diversity contributing marginally on perception-bound tasks.
falsifiable_prediction: Encoder-diverse ensembles capture at least 70% of the full-diversity gain while LLM-diverse ensembles capture at most 30%. KILL: the claim dies if LLM diversity matches or exceeds encoder diversity in captured gain on perception-bound tasks.
why_important: Diversity is expensive (multiple deployments); knowing the effective axis lets builders buy decorrelation where it works and skip where it does not — a direct cost-reliability lever.
why_possibly_novel: MODEL SPECULATION (unverified): ensemble diversity theory is classical; the encoder-vs-LLM factorial attribution for multimodal agent ensembles may be unmeasured.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Assemble open VLMs permitting the 2x2 factorial (shared and different encoders/LLMs); run voting ensembles per cell on perception-bound public benchmarks; decompose gains by factor.
main_risk: Truly encoder-swapped model pairs are limited among open VLMs; partial confounds between encoder and training recipe need acknowledgment.
community_default_belief: Agent diversity is generic — different models disagree usefully regardless of where they differ.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Two agents sharing eyes share their blindness; language-side diversity rephrases the same mistake rather than challenging it.
fastest_falsification_experiment: One day, single GPU: 3-4 open VLMs forming partial factorial, voting comparison on 300 instances. Public data only.

evidence_label.falsifiable_prediction: EXPECTED RESULT (pre-registered threshold; no measured numbers)
evidence_label.prior_work_basis: VERIFIED PRIOR WORK (well-known): ensemble diversity theory is classical; the multimodal factorial attribution is MODEL SPECULATION.

one_line_idea: Role prompts change transcripts, not outcomes: skeptic/looker/reasoner roles only improve multi-agent vision accuracy when the roles receive different inputs, so engineered information asymmetry — not persona text — is the active ingredient.
problem: Multi-agent systems assign personas expecting functional specialization, but a persona prompt over identical inputs may produce only stylistic variation while the systems' cost triples.
core_hypothesis: Functional specialization requires informational specialization: giving the 'skeptic' only the image and the bare claim (not the proposer's reasoning), and the 'looker' only crops (not the question history), creates genuinely decorrelated judgments that persona text alone cannot, converting role-play into measurable division of labor.
falsifiable_prediction: Persona prompts over identical inputs gain at most 1 point over identical agents; the same personas with engineered input asymmetry gain at least 3 points at equal compute. KILL: the claim dies if persona-only gains reach 3 points (role text alone suffices).
why_important: It gives multi-agent design a working principle — allocate information, not adjectives — and debunks the cheapest and most common form of agent theater if persona-only fails.
why_possibly_novel: MODEL SPECULATION (unverified): role-play multi-agent systems are popular; a controlled persona-vs-information-asymmetry factorial in vision settings may be new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Implement 3-agent teams in four conditions (persona x input-asymmetry factorial) over open VLMs; evaluate at matched total compute on public benchmarks; attribute gains to factors.
main_risk: Input restriction can starve an agent of necessary context, so asymmetry designs must be validated as individually non-crippling.
community_default_belief: Assigning distinct roles to agents produces division of labor; the persona shapes the computation.
why_it_might_be_wrong: A model conditioned on the same evidence samples from nearly the same distribution regardless of its nametag; only different evidence forces different conclusions.
fastest_falsification_experiment: One day, single GPU: 200 instances, 4 conditions, factorial attribution. Public data only.

evidence_label.community_default_belief: MODEL SPECULATION (inferred from persona-based system designs)
evidence_label.falsifiable_prediction: EXPECTED RESULT (pre-registered threshold; no measured numbers)
evidence_label.prior_work_basis: MODEL SPECULATION: role-play multi-agent systems exist; the persona-vs-asymmetry factorial is unverified.

one_line_idea: At matched inference compute, majority voting matches debate and judge-arbitration on perception tasks: the deliberation transcript is compute repackaged, and reported protocol advantages vanish under iso-compute accounting.
problem: Coordination protocols (debate, arbitration, discussion rounds) are compared against single agents rather than against the same compute spent on the simplest aggregation, so protocol sophistication and raw compute are confounded in every claim.
core_hypothesis: On perception-bound tasks, deliberation between agents does not create information that independent sampling plus voting lacks; equalizing total compute across protocols will compress their differences to noise, revealing transcript exchange as an expensive no-op.
falsifiable_prediction: Across three perception task families at matched compute, the spread between voting, debate, and judge-arbitration is at most 1.5 points. KILL: the claim dies if any deliberation protocol beats matched-compute voting by 4+ points.
why_important: Deliberation protocols carry engineering complexity, latency, and failure modes; if they are voting in costume, the field can delete a layer of machinery from deployed systems.
why_possibly_novel: MODEL SPECULATION (unverified): individual protocol papers exist; a matched-compute protocol equivalence study on perception tasks may be missing.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Implement the three protocols over the same open VLM with careful token accounting; equalize total compute per instance; evaluate across three public perception task families with variance-aware statistics.
main_risk: Compute equalization has freedom (more voters vs more rounds); the study must sweep configurations per protocol and compare fronts, not single points.
community_default_belief: Deliberation adds error-correction beyond independent aggregation; debate is more than expensive voting.
why_it_might_be_wrong: For percept-level questions, agents have nothing to teach each other — their messages carry conclusions, not new evidence, so exchanging them cannot outperform pooling conclusions directly.
fastest_falsification_experiment: One day, single GPU: one task family, three protocols at one matched budget, spread estimate. Public data only.

evidence_label.falsifiable_prediction: EXPECTED RESULT (pre-registered threshold; no measured numbers)
evidence_label.prior_work_basis: MODEL SPECULATION: protocol papers exist separately; matched-compute equivalence testing unverified.

one_line_idea: An adversarial checker agent instructed to construct the disconfirming view — the specific crop or transformation that would falsify the claim — beats confirmation-style verification at equal cost, importing falsification-seeking into vision loops.
problem: Verification agents ask 'is this right?' — a confirmation-biased query that models answer agreeably; nothing in current loops searches for the observation that would prove the claim wrong.
core_hypothesis: Falsification is an actionable visual strategy: for claims like 'there are three cups' or 'the sign says stop', there exists a specific view (crop, zoom, contrast change) most likely to reveal the claim false if it is; an agent trained by instruction to construct and execute that view detects more errors than one asked to double-check, at the same budget.
falsifiable_prediction: The falsification-seeking checker improves error detection by at least 10 points over confirmation-style checking at equal compute, with the advantage concentrated on false claims. KILL: the claim dies if the improvement is 3 points or less.
why_important: It operationalizes a core scientific norm as a loop mechanism, and its success would define a reusable checker role for any multimodal pipeline — the agent whose job is to break the answer.
why_possibly_novel: MODEL SPECULATION (unverified): adversarial examples target models with gradients; instruction-driven adversarial evidence search inside agent loops may be new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Build claim sets with controlled truth values on public images; implement confirmation vs falsification checker prompts with identical view budgets; compare detection rates and view choices.
main_risk: The falsifier may manufacture misleading views (extreme crops that hide true content), flipping true claims; retraction precision must be tracked.
community_default_belief: Checking means having another look or another model confirm; seeking disconfirmation is not part of the verification toolbox.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Confirmation queries sample the same agreeable mode; only a query whose success criterion is finding the flaw changes the search objective.
fastest_falsification_experiment: One day, single GPU: 200 claims (half false), both checkers, detection comparison. Public data only.

evidence_label.community_default_belief: MODEL SPECULATION (inferred from confirmation-style verification practice)
evidence_label.falsifiable_prediction: EXPECTED RESULT (pre-registered threshold; no measured numbers)
evidence_label.prior_work_basis: MODEL SPECULATION: gradient-based adversarial methods exist; instruction-driven falsification search unverified.

one_line_idea: Hallucinated details become sticky in multi-agent transcripts: once an unsupported visual claim is repeated twice, its adoption probability by other agents exceeds its correction probability, quantifying error contagion as a system property.
problem: Multi-agent pipelines share a transcript that functions as collective memory, but nothing tracks how unsupported claims propagate through it — whether agents treat repetition as corroboration.
core_hypothesis: Transcript repetition manufactures credibility: the probability that a downstream agent adopts an unsupported claim rises with each repetition, crossing the probability of correction after about two mentions, so pipelines have a measurable contagion threshold beyond which errors become collectively locked in.
falsifiable_prediction: After 2 repetitions, adoption probability of injected unsupported claims is at least 2x the correction probability, and adoption grows monotonically with repetition count. KILL: the claim dies if correction stays at or above adoption regardless of repetitions.
why_important: Contagion dynamics determine whether multi-agent systems dampen or amplify individual errors — the central safety question for agent teams, currently unmeasured for vision.
why_possibly_novel: MODEL SPECULATION (unverified): rumor propagation is studied in social networks; controlled claim-injection contagion measurement inside multimodal agent pipelines may be new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Inject controlled unsupported claims into transcripts at varying repetition counts across multi-agent configurations on public images; measure downstream adoption vs correction rates per repetition level.
main_risk: Injection realism: claims planted artificially may be phrased unlike organic agent errors; a subset should use harvested natural hallucinations.
community_default_belief: More agents reviewing a transcript means more chances someone catches the error.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Each agent reads repetition as independent confirmation because nothing marks the claims' common origin — the transcript launders one error into consensus.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Half a day, single GPU: 200 injection episodes at 3 repetition levels, adoption-vs-correction curves. Public data only.

evidence_label.falsifiable_prediction: EXPECTED RESULT (pre-registered threshold; no measured numbers)
evidence_label.prior_work_basis: MODEL SPECULATION: social contagion literature exists; agent-transcript contagion measurement unverified.

one_line_idea: Splitting dense scenes among parallel agents pays only above a measurable object-density threshold: below it, coordination and double-counting costs exceed parallel gains, and the crossover is predictable from single-agent working-set limits.
problem: Spatial division of labor (each agent takes an image region) is an obvious parallelization for dense tasks, but merging partial results creates boundary errors and duplicates whose cost has never been traded off against the parallel gain.
core_hypothesis: Partitioned processing helps exactly when single-agent capacity saturates: the crossover density where partitioning starts to win coincides with the single agent's measured working-set limit, making the deployment decision predictable from a cheap single-agent measurement rather than from full system A/B tests.
falsifiable_prediction: Partitioned agents lose to a single agent by at least 2 points below the predicted density threshold and win above it, with the empirical crossover within 30% of the working-set-derived prediction. KILL: the claim dies if partitioning uniformly helps or uniformly hurts across densities.
why_important: It links two system parameters (working-set capacity, task density) into a predictive deployment rule — an example of agent-system design maturing from trial-and-error to engineering.
why_possibly_novel: MODEL SPECULATION (unverified): divide-and-conquer image processing is standard; a capacity-derived crossover prediction for agent teams on dense counting/description tasks may be new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Measure a single agent's working-set limit; run single vs 4-way partitioned teams on public dense scenes stratified by density; locate the empirical crossover and compare against prediction. Use counting error and description-completeness metrics.
main_risk: Boundary-object handling policy dominates partitioned performance; it must be fixed and reported as part of the protocol.
community_default_belief: Parallelizing over image regions is a free win for dense scenes, like tiling in classical detection.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Classical tiling merges geometry; agent merging reconciles narratives, and narrative reconciliation adds errors tiles never had.
fastest_falsification_experiment: One day, single GPU: density-stratified 200 scenes, single vs partitioned, crossover check. Public data only.

evidence_label.falsifiable_prediction: EXPECTED RESULT (pre-registered threshold; no measured numbers)
evidence_label.prior_work_basis: VERIFIED PRIOR WORK (well-known): tiled inference is standard in detection; the agent-team crossover law is MODEL SPECULATION.

one_line_idea: Tool-set diversity decorrelates agent errors where temperature and prompt diversity do not: assigning different tool access to ensemble members lowers error correlation and lifts ensemble accuracy beyond any sampling-based diversity at equal cost.
problem: Ensembles need decorrelated errors, but the cheap diversity knobs (temperature, prompt paraphrase) only jitter the decoder around the same evidence; the ensemble sees one percept many times.
core_hypothesis: Diversity must enter through evidence, not sampling: members with different tool access (one zooms, one reads text, one queries structure) make errors in different places, and measured pairwise error correlation — the quantity that governs ensemble gains — drops substantially only under tool-set diversity.
falsifiable_prediction: Tool-set diversity reduces mean pairwise error correlation by at least 0.15 and adds at least 2 points over temperature-diverse ensembles at equal total compute. KILL: the claim dies if the correlation drop is 0.05 or less (tool diversity fails to decorrelate).
why_important: It identifies the actionable diversity axis for multimodal ensembles and replaces cargo-cult temperature sweeps with an evidence-allocation design rule.
why_possibly_novel: MODEL SPECULATION (unverified): ensemble theory ties gains to error correlation; deliberately inducing decorrelation via heterogeneous tool access in agent ensembles may be new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Build ensembles under three diversity regimes (temperature, prompt, tool-set) at matched compute over one open VLM; measure pairwise error correlations and ensemble accuracy on public benchmarks.
main_risk: Restricting tools can lower individual member accuracy enough to offset decorrelation gains; the net effect is the honest test.
community_default_belief: Ensemble diversity is achieved by sampling settings; architecture and evidence access are held fixed for comparability.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Correlated evidence makes correlated errors mathematically inevitable; no decoder jitter can undo what the shared percept already decided.
fastest_falsification_experiment: One day, single GPU: 3 regimes, 300 instances, correlation and accuracy comparison. Public data only.

evidence_label.falsifiable_prediction: EXPECTED RESULT (pre-registered threshold; no measured numbers)
evidence_label.prior_work_basis: VERIFIED PRIOR WORK (well-known): error-correlation ensemble theory is classical; tool-access diversity engineering is MODEL SPECULATION.

one_line_idea: Manager-worker hierarchies only beat flat self-verification when workers use different tools or views: a manager reviewing same-tool worker outputs is redundant compute, and the condition can be tested by toggling worker heterogeneity.
problem: Hierarchical agent architectures add a manager layer by default, but the manager's review can only add value if workers bring it decision-relevant differences to arbitrate — a precondition designs never check.
core_hypothesis: The manager's marginal value is a function of worker output diversity: with homogeneous workers the manager sees near-identical reports and its review is a costly identity operation, while heterogeneous workers (different tools/views) give the manager real arbitration work; toggling heterogeneity at fixed compute isolates this.
falsifiable_prediction: Hierarchy gains at least 3 points over flat verification with heterogeneous workers and at most 1 point with homogeneous workers at matched compute. KILL: the claim dies if homogeneous-worker hierarchy gains 3+ points (managers add value beyond arbitration).
why_important: Hierarchies are becoming a default architecture pattern; a precondition test prevents paying manager overhead where it provably cannot help.
why_possibly_novel: MODEL SPECULATION (unverified): hierarchical agent systems are popular in engineering; a controlled heterogeneity-toggle isolating the manager's value-condition may be new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Implement flat and hierarchical configurations with worker heterogeneity on/off at matched compute over public tasks; attribute the hierarchy's gain to the heterogeneity factor.
main_risk: Manager prompt quality confounds the architecture comparison; the manager must be identical across heterogeneity conditions.
community_default_belief: A supervisory agent reviewing worker outputs adds a layer of quality control that generally helps.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Review without difference is rubber-stamping; the manager can arbitrate only where workers disagree for reasons.
fastest_falsification_experiment: One day, single GPU: 200 instances, 4 conditions (flat/hierarchy x homo/hetero), gain attribution. Public data only.

evidence_label.falsifiable_prediction: EXPECTED RESULT (pre-registered threshold; no measured numbers)
evidence_label.prior_work_basis: MODEL SPECULATION: hierarchical agent engineering exists; the value-condition isolation is unverified.

family_fingerprint.measurement_family: hierarchy gain attribution at matched compute

one_line_idea: In multi-agent vision exchanges, message confidence markers predict claim adoption more than attached image evidence does: agents weigh rhetoric over pixels, making persuasive-but-wrong agents systematically dangerous in mixed pipelines.
problem: Agent-to-agent messages mix rhetorical style (hedges, assertiveness) with evidential content (attached crops, cited regions), and receiving agents must weigh both — but nothing measures which actually drives belief adoption in the pipeline.
core_hypothesis: Adoption of claims by receiving agents is governed more by linguistic confidence than by evidential attachment: in a factorial manipulation (confident/hedged phrasing x evidence attached/absent), the phrasing coefficient will dominate the evidence coefficient, exposing a systematic vulnerability to persuasive error.
falsifiable_prediction: In adoption regressions over the factorial, the confidence-marker coefficient is at least 2x the evidence-attachment coefficient. KILL: the claim dies if evidence attachment dominates phrasing (agents are evidence-weighers after all).
why_important: If rhetoric beats evidence, any multi-agent system is only as reliable as its most overconfident member, and message-format standards (mandatory evidence, stripped rhetoric) become safety-critical.
why_possibly_novel: MODEL SPECULATION (unverified): sycophancy and persuasion are studied for human-model interaction; a rhetoric-vs-evidence factorial for inter-agent visual claims may be new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Construct inter-agent messages about public images in the 2x2 factorial with controlled truth values; measure receiving-agent adoption rates per cell; fit the adoption regression.
main_risk: Confidence phrasing may correlate with truth in natural transcripts; the factorial's forced decoupling is the point but limits ecological validity.
community_default_belief: Agents evaluate incoming claims on content; attached evidence is the strongest content there is.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Models are trained on human text where assertive claims are usually true; they inherit the assertiveness-equals-truth prior, and checking attached pixels is work the receiving agent can skip.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Half a day, single GPU: 400 factorial messages, adoption regression. Public data only.

evidence_label.falsifiable_prediction: EXPECTED RESULT (pre-registered threshold; no measured numbers)
evidence_label.prior_work_basis: VERIFIED PRIOR WORK (well-known): sycophancy studies exist for human-model interaction; the inter-agent factorial is MODEL SPECULATION.

one_line_idea: VLM-judge failures decompose into perception failures (cannot see the difference) and criterion failures (sees it, wrong rubric): an oracle-perception protocol — feeding ground-truth descriptions instead of pixels — cleanly splits the two and tells you whether to fix eyes or rubric.
problem: VLM judges disagree with humans for reasons nobody can currently separate: the judge may not perceive the relevant difference between outputs, or may perceive it and weigh it wrong — two failures with opposite remedies.
core_hypothesis: Substituting verified textual descriptions of the compared items for the images themselves removes the perception load while preserving the judgment task; the disagreement that disappears under substitution is perception-borne, the remainder is criterion-borne, giving a reusable decomposition instrument for any judging task.
falsifiable_prediction: On perception-heavy judging tasks, oracle-perception substitution recovers at least 50% of judge-human disagreement; on style-preference tasks it recovers under 20%. KILL: the claim dies if substitution recovers under 15% on perception-heavy tasks (decomposition uninformative).
why_important: The decomposition dictates investment: perception-borne failure means better eyes or rendered evidence; criterion-borne means rubric engineering — currently teams guess, and the instrument replaces guessing.
why_possibly_novel: MODEL SPECULATION (unverified): judge reliability is usually reported as a single agreement number; a perception/criterion decomposition protocol via oracle substitution may be new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: On public judging datasets with human labels, create verified descriptions of compared outputs; run judges on pixels vs descriptions; decompose disagreement by task type.
main_risk: Descriptions may leak the intended verdict, deflating apparent criterion failure; description construction needs verdict-blind authorship.
community_default_belief: Judge quality is one number — agreement with humans — and it improves with model scale.
why_it_might_be_wrong: A single agreement number conflates two orthogonal capabilities that scale differently: perception improves with encoders, criteria improve with instructions.
fastest_falsification_experiment: One day, single GPU: 200 judging items with human labels, both input conditions, disagreement decomposition. Public data only.

evidence_label.community_default_belief: MODEL SPECULATION (inferred from single-number judge reporting)
evidence_label.falsifiable_prediction: EXPECTED RESULT (pre-registered threshold; no measured numbers)
evidence_label.prior_work_basis: VERIFIED PRIOR WORK (well-known): LLM-as-judge protocols exist for text; the perception/criterion decomposition is MODEL SPECULATION.

one_line_idea: The generator-verifier gap that powers self-improvement in code and math is absent for perception: judging a visual answer requires the same percept as producing it, so same-model visual judges provide no exploitable training signal.
problem: Self-improvement recipes assume verification is easier than generation, so a model can judge its own outputs into a training signal; whether that asymmetry exists for perception at all is untested and load-bearing for multimodal self-training plans.
core_hypothesis: For perception-bound tasks there is no verification shortcut: the judge must re-perform the same perceptual computation as the generator, so same-model judge accuracy tracks generator accuracy instead of exceeding it, and the exploitable gap that drives code/math self-improvement is structurally missing.
falsifiable_prediction: Same-model judge accuracy exceeds generator accuracy by at most 2 points on perception-bound tasks, while a matched code-style control shows a gap of 10+ points. KILL: the claim dies if the visual judge exceeds its generator by 10+ points (a real verification shortcut exists).
why_important: It predicts which self-improvement pipelines can work for multimodal models: without a generator-verifier gap, same-model visual RLAIF recycles noise, and progress requires external or decorrelated verification.
why_possibly_novel: MODEL SPECULATION (unverified): the verification-easier-than-generation asymmetry is folklore for reasoning domains; a direct measurement of its absence for perception may be new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: For matched task pairs (perception-bound visual QA vs checkable symbolic tasks), measure generation accuracy and same-model judging accuracy on the same items; compare gap structures across domains.
main_risk: Judging format (pairwise vs absolute) affects measured judge accuracy; both formats should be tested to make the gap comparison robust.
community_default_belief: Verification is generally easier than generation, so model-as-judge bootstrapping transfers to multimodal settings.
why_it_might_be_wrong: The asymmetry comes from domains with cheap independent checks (run the code, check the proof); perception has no analog — seeing that an answer is right is the same act as seeing the answer.
fastest_falsification_experiment: One day, single GPU: 300 items per domain, generation vs judging accuracy, gap comparison. Public data only.

evidence_label.community_default_belief: MODEL SPECULATION (inferred from self-improvement recipe transfer)
evidence_label.falsifiable_prediction: EXPECTED RESULT (pre-registered threshold; no measured numbers)
evidence_label.prior_work_basis: MODEL SPECULATION: verification-gap folklore exists for reasoning; the perception-domain measurement is unverified.

one_line_idea: Judges given executable rubrics — per-item binary checks each requiring pointed image evidence — agree with humans more than holistic judges at equal cost, converting judging from perception-plus-taste into a sequence of verifiable micro-perceptions.
problem: Holistic judging asks one opaque question (which output is better?) that entangles many small perceptual checks with unstated preferences; the judge's capability is wasted on tasks it could do well if they were asked separately.
core_hypothesis: Decomposing judgment into an executable rubric (does output A mislabel any object? does it miss the requested attribute? — each answered with a pointed region) converts one hard judgment into several easy perceptions, raising human agreement at matched compute and making judge verdicts auditable item by item.
falsifiable_prediction: Rubric-executing judges gain at least 10 points of human agreement over holistic judges at equal compute on grounded judging tasks. KILL: the claim dies if the gain is 3 points or less (decomposition overhead eats the benefit).
why_important: Reliable VLM judging is a capability bottleneck for evaluation and for reward signals; a format-level fix that buys double-digit agreement without new models changes both uses immediately.
why_possibly_novel: MODEL SPECULATION (unverified): checklist evaluation exists in NLP; executable evidence-pointing rubrics for visual judging with agreement accounting may be new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Author rubrics for two public judging task types; run holistic vs rubric-executing judges at matched compute; score against human majority labels; audit rubric-item verdicts against pointed evidence.
main_risk: Rubric authorship becomes the new bottleneck and could encode the author's biases at scale; rubric-generation by models needs separate validation.
community_default_belief: Judging quality is a model capability; you improve it with stronger judges, not with question formats.
why_it_might_be_wrong: The format determines which capability is exercised: holistic questions invoke taste, rubric items invoke perception — and current models are far better at the second.
fastest_falsification_experiment: One day, single GPU: 200 judging items, both formats, agreement comparison. Public data only.

evidence_label.falsifiable_prediction: EXPECTED RESULT (pre-registered threshold; no measured numbers)
evidence_label.prior_work_basis: MODEL SPECULATION: checklist evaluation exists in NLP; visual executable rubrics unverified.

one_line_idea: Position and order biases in visual pairwise judging can be converted from a flaw into a filter: keeping only swap-consistent judgments yields a subset with much higher human agreement, giving a usable reliability lever without retraining.
problem: Pairwise visual judges are known to flip verdicts when presentation order swaps; the standard response is averaging or despair, but the flip signal itself may identify exactly which judgments are trustworthy.
core_hypothesis: Swap-inconsistency marks low-information judgments: verdicts stable under presentation swap are the ones grounded in perceived content differences, so filtering to the swap-consistent subset trades coverage for a large, quantifiable reliability gain — a capability recovered from a bias.
falsifiable_prediction: The swap-consistent subset (expected to be the majority of pairs) shows at least 10 points higher human agreement than the full set, and inconsistent pairs cluster near human-disagreement cases. KILL: the claim dies if the consistency filter adds 3 points or less, or retains under 40% of pairs.
why_important: Practitioners need reliability now, from the judges that exist; a filter that upgrades reliability with two inference calls per pair is deployable everywhere judges are used.
why_possibly_novel: MODEL SPECULATION (unverified): position bias in judging is documented; using swap-consistency as a per-judgment reliability certificate with agreement accounting may be new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Run pairwise judgments in both orders on public human-labeled comparison sets; partition by consistency; compare human agreement and analyze what content properties predict inconsistency.
main_risk: Consistency may select easy pairs, making the filter a difficulty detector rather than a reliability upgrade on hard pairs; report agreement stratified by difficulty.
community_default_belief: Order bias is noise to be averaged out by randomizing presentation.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Averaging discards the information in the flip: a verdict that survives the swap carries evidence the average of two coin flips does not.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Half a day, single GPU: 300 labeled pairs, both orders, filtered-agreement comparison. Public data only.

evidence_label.falsifiable_prediction: EXPECTED RESULT (pre-registered threshold; no measured numbers)
evidence_label.prior_work_basis: VERIFIED PRIOR WORK (well-known): position bias in LLM judging is documented; the consistency-filter capability claim is MODEL SPECULATION.

one_line_idea: Visual-judge self-preference is stylistic, not substantive: rewriting identical answer content in another model family's style moves judge preference, showing the bias lives in surface-form recognition rather than content assessment.
problem: Judges preferring their own family's outputs corrupts every self-evaluated leaderboard, but the mechanism is unknown: do judges prefer their family's content decisions or its prose fingerprint?
core_hypothesis: Self-preference is carried by style: holding answer content fixed (same claims, same regions, same verdicts) while transplanting the surface style of another family will move the judge's preference by nearly as much as swapping actual content producers — localizing the bias to recognizable form.
falsifiable_prediction: Style transplantation shifts preference rates by at least 10 points despite content-matched pairs. KILL: the claim dies if style-only manipulation shifts preference by 3 points or less (bias is substantive, not stylistic).
why_important: If the bias is stylistic, it is removable by style normalization before judging — a cheap fix; if substantive, self-judging is fundamentally compromised. The experiment decides which world we are in.
why_possibly_novel: MODEL SPECULATION (unverified): self-preference is documented for LLM judges; a content-controlled style-transplant localization for visual judges may be new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Generate content-matched answer pairs about public images; use paraphrase models to transplant family styles; run family judges over the style factorial; regress preference on style vs content origin.
main_risk: Verifying true content-match after paraphrase is hard; requires claim-level equivalence checks on every transplanted pair.
community_default_belief: Self-preference reflects genuine agreement with one's own reasoning style and content choices — an inherent evaluator conflict.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Models are strong recognizers of their own token statistics; familiarity masquerades as quality without any content judgment occurring.
fastest_falsification_experiment: One day, single GPU: 200 content-matched pairs, style factorial, preference regression. Public data only.

evidence_label.falsifiable_prediction: EXPECTED RESULT (pre-registered threshold; no measured numbers)
evidence_label.prior_work_basis: VERIFIED PRIOR WORK (well-known): self-preference reports exist for LLM judges; the style-localization claim is MODEL SPECULATION.

one_line_idea: Ensembles of small diverse judges beat one frontier judge at matched cost only when their vision encoders differ: judge-ensemble value is a decorrelation phenomenon, predictable from pairwise judge error correlations before deployment.
problem: Evaluation budgets force a choice between one expensive judge and several cheap ones, and the field lacks a predictive rule for when the ensemble side of that trade wins.
core_hypothesis: Judge ensembles obey the same decorrelation law as task ensembles: aggregate judging quality is predicted by mean pairwise error correlation, which is low only across encoder families — so the cheap-ensemble option wins exactly when encoder diversity is available, and the pre-deployment correlation measurement predicts the winner.
falsifiable_prediction: Encoder-diverse small-judge ensembles match or beat the frontier judge at matched cost, while same-encoder ensembles lose by at least 3 points of human agreement; pre-measured error correlation predicts the outcome with rank fidelity. KILL: the claim dies if same-encoder ensembles match diverse ones (correlation is not the mechanism).
why_important: Evaluation at scale is constrained by judge cost; a validated cheap-ensemble recipe with a pre-deployment predictor changes how the community buys judgment.
why_possibly_novel: MODEL SPECULATION (unverified): jury-of-judges ideas exist for text; the encoder-diversity condition and correlation-based predictability for visual judging may be new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Assemble small open VLM judges spanning encoder families; measure pairwise error correlations on pilot items; compare ensemble configurations against a large judge at matched cost on human-labeled sets.
main_risk: Cost matching between one large and several small judges is deployment-dependent (latency vs throughput); report both accountings.
community_default_belief: The best judge is the strongest single model you can afford.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Judging error, like task error, cancels only across decorrelated instruments — and a strong judge is still one instrument.
fastest_falsification_experiment: One day, single GPU: 3 small judges + 1 large, 300 labeled items, matched-cost comparison. Public data only.

evidence_label.falsifiable_prediction: EXPECTED RESULT (pre-registered threshold; no measured numbers)
evidence_label.prior_work_basis: MODEL SPECULATION: jury-of-judges ideas exist for text; encoder-diversity condition unverified.

one_line_idea: Reference-based visual judging penalizes correct-but-different answers: judges overweight surface similarity to the reference, and the penalty on verified-equivalent paraphrases is large enough to flip system rankings that depend on judge scores.
problem: Reference-guided judging is the default protocol for visual QA and captioning evaluation, assuming the reference anchors correctness; but the anchor may reward reference-likeness rather than image-groundedness.
core_hypothesis: Judges given references shift from image-grounded assessment to text-matching: verified-equivalent answers phrased unlike the reference lose points that identical-content reference-like phrasings keep, and the effect size is large enough to reorder systems whose outputs differ in phrasing style.
falsifiable_prediction: Verified-equivalent paraphrases lose at least 10 points of judge score relative to reference-matching phrasings of the same content, and simulated leaderboards with style-differing systems flip rankings under reference-based versus reference-free judging. KILL: the claim dies if the paraphrase penalty is 3 points or less.
why_important: Reference anchoring would systematically penalize models with different (possibly better) description styles, and every reference-judged multimodal comparison inherits that distortion.
why_possibly_novel: MODEL SPECULATION (unverified): reference bias is discussed for text metrics; a verified-equivalence paraphrase audit of reference-guided VLM judging with ranking-flip accounting may be new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Build verified-equivalent paraphrase sets for answers on public benchmarks; run reference-based and reference-free judges on both phrasings; measure the penalty and simulate ranking effects.
main_risk: Verifying true equivalence is the hard part; equivalence must be established by claim decomposition, not by another judge.
community_default_belief: Providing the reference makes judging more accurate by anchoring it to ground truth.
why_it_might_be_wrong: The reference is one phrasing of the truth, not the truth; a text-matching shortcut to it is cheaper than looking at the image, and models take cheap shortcuts.
fastest_falsification_experiment: One day, single GPU: 200 verified paraphrase pairs, both judging modes, penalty estimate. Public data only.

evidence_label.community_default_belief: MODEL SPECULATION (inferred from reference-guided protocol defaults)
evidence_label.falsifiable_prediction: EXPECTED RESULT (pre-registered threshold; no measured numbers)
evidence_label.prior_work_basis: MODEL SPECULATION: reference-bias discussions exist for text metrics; the visual judging audit is unverified.

family_fingerprint.manipulated_variable: phrasing similarity to reference at fixed content

one_line_idea: VLM judges fail on dense geometric outputs but recover with rendered comparisons: overlaying prediction-vs-reference differences as visual diffs lifts judge accuracy on box and keypoint quality far above judging from raw pairs, mapping a capability boundary and its fix.
problem: Judges are increasingly asked to score spatial outputs (which detection set is better, which pose is more accurate), a task requiring simultaneous comparison of many small geometric relations — plausibly beyond raw side-by-side inspection.
core_hypothesis: The failure is presentational: raw side-by-side geometric comparison overloads the judge, but rendering the disagreement itself (color-coded diff overlays marking added/missing/shifted elements) converts the task into perception of highlighted differences, recovering most of the gap to geometric-metric ground truth.
falsifiable_prediction: Diff-rendered judging lifts agreement with geometric ground truth by at least 15 points over raw-pair judging on box/keypoint quality tasks. KILL: the claim dies if the lift is 5 points or less (the failure is not presentational).
why_important: Geometric judging with human-meaningful justifications would complement threshold-based metrics where they are least informative (near-misses, structured errors), and the diff-rendering principle generalizes to any structured output.
why_possibly_novel: MODEL SPECULATION (unverified): visual diffs are a developer-tool concept; systematic diff-rendering as a judge-capability intervention with boundary mapping may be new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Construct box/keypoint output pairs with known quality orderings from public detection/pose data; run judges on raw pairs vs diff renders; map accuracy by error magnitude and clutter level.
main_risk: Diff rendering presupposes alignment between the two outputs; ambiguous correspondence cases may need the very judgment being tested.
community_default_belief: Geometric quality is what IoU-style metrics are for; VLM judges are for semantics, and their geometric weakness is inherent.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Humans also fail raw side-by-side geometric comparison but succeed instantly with highlighted diffs; the capability may be presentation-limited, not model-limited.
fastest_falsification_experiment: One day, single GPU: 300 constructed pairs, both presentations, agreement with geometric ground truth. Public data only.

evidence_label.community_default_belief: MODEL SPECULATION (inferred from metric-vs-judge division of labor)
evidence_label.falsifiable_prediction: EXPECTED RESULT (pre-registered threshold; no measured numbers)
evidence_label.prior_work_basis: MODEL SPECULATION: visual-diff tooling exists for developers; judge-capability intervention unverified.

one_line_idea: Using a VLM judge as a training reward has a measurable hacking onset: as optimization pressure grows, policies exploit judge blind spots at a predictable point, and the onset is a property of the judge-policy pair estimable before full training.
problem: VLM judges are becoming reward models for visual policies, importing the known reward-hacking failure mode with no tooling to predict when a given judge will start being gamed.
core_hypothesis: Hacking onset is systematic: as optimization pressure (divergence from the initial policy) increases, judge score and true quality first rise together, then diverge at a pressure threshold characteristic of the judge-policy pair — and a cheap probe (scoring deliberately style-perturbed outputs to map the judge's blind-spot directions) predicts that threshold without running full training.
falsifiable_prediction: Judge score and human-assessed quality diverge by at least 3 points beyond some pressure level in every run, and the probe-predicted onset correlates with realized onset at rho of at least 0.5 across judge-policy pairs. KILL: the claim dies if no divergence appears across the pressure sweep, or the probe has no predictive power (rho under 0.2).
why_important: A pre-training hacking forecast tells teams how hard they can optimize against a given judge safely — turning a known catastrophic failure mode into a budgeted engineering parameter.
why_possibly_novel: MODEL SPECULATION (unverified): reward hacking is documented for text RLHF; onset predictability from blind-spot probes for visual judge rewards may be new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: LoRA-tune small open policies against open VLM judges at increasing KL budgets on a captioning-style task; score checkpoints with held-out human labels; fit onset points and test the probe's predictions.
main_risk: Human quality assessment at many checkpoints is the expensive component; use small stratified samples with agreement checks.
community_default_belief: Stronger judges are safe rewards; hacking is a problem of weak or narrow reward models.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Every judge has blind-spot directions, and optimization is a blind-spot-seeking process; strength moves the onset but does not remove it.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Three single-GPU days: one policy, one judge, 4 pressure levels, small human-labeled checkpoint audit. Public data and open models only.

evidence_label.falsifiable_prediction: EXPECTED RESULT (pre-registered threshold; no measured numbers)
evidence_label.prior_work_basis: VERIFIED PRIOR WORK (well-known): reward hacking is documented in RLHF settings; the onset-predictability claim is MODEL SPECULATION.

one_line_idea: Pairwise visual-judgment intransitivity is a cheap reliability meter: cycle rate in a small tournament predicts judge-human agreement without any human labels, and cycle-repaired rankings recover accuracy the raw judge lacks.
problem: Assessing a judge normally requires human labels, which defeats the purpose of having a judge; the field needs label-free reliability signals computable from the judge's own behavior.
core_hypothesis: Preference cycles (A beats B beats C beats A) are logical inconsistencies whose frequency tracks the judge's noise level: cycle rate measured on a small round-robin correlates with human agreement across judges and tasks, and fitting a consistent global ranking through the cycles yields better orderings than raw pairwise verdicts.
falsifiable_prediction: Across judges and tasks, tournament cycle rate rank-correlates with independently measured human agreement at rho of at least 0.5, and cycle-repaired rankings gain at least 5 points of ranking accuracy over raw judgments. KILL: the claim dies if the correlation is under 0.2 (cycles do not track reliability).
why_important: A label-free reliability meter enables judge selection, monitoring, and drift detection in production evaluation systems where human audits are sparse or absent.
why_possibly_novel: MODEL SPECULATION (unverified): intransitivity is noted anecdotally in LLM judging; validating cycle rate as a quantitative label-free reliability predictor for visual judges may be new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Run round-robin tournaments over output sets from public benchmarks with several open VLM judges; measure cycle rates; separately measure human agreement on samples; test the correlation and the repair gain.
main_risk: Cycle rate may saturate (near zero or near random) for very strong or very weak judges, compressing the usable dynamic range.
community_default_belief: Judge quality can only be assessed against human labels; the judge's internal consistency is not evidence of its accuracy.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Logical consistency is a necessary condition for tracking a real quality ordering; measuring how badly it fails bounds how much signal can be present.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Half a day, single GPU: 8-item tournaments x 30 sets x 2 judges, cycle rates vs sampled human agreement. Public data only.

evidence_label.community_default_belief: MODEL SPECULATION (inferred from label-dependent evaluation practice)
evidence_label.falsifiable_prediction: EXPECTED RESULT (pre-registered threshold; no measured numbers)
evidence_label.prior_work_basis: MODEL SPECULATION: intransitivity anecdotes exist; quantitative label-free validation unverified.

one_line_idea: End-to-end agent success is worse than the product of per-step success rates: shared context couples steps so that errors interact super-multiplicatively, and the negative interaction term grows with chain length.
problem: Reliability engineering for pipelines assumes independent stage failures (multiply the success rates), and agent designers inherit that mental model — but agent steps share a transcript, which correlates their failures.
core_hypothesis: Context coupling makes step failures mutually reinforcing: a marginal early step degrades the context all later steps condition on, so observed end-to-end success falls below the independence prediction by a coupling term that is measurable per pipeline and grows with depth.
falsifiable_prediction: Observed k-step success undershoots the independence prediction (product of individually measured step success rates) by at least 5 points at k of 4 or more. KILL: the claim dies if observed success is within 2 points of the product prediction across depths.
why_important: System-level reliability forecasting from component tests is how engineering disciplines scale; knowing the coupling correction (and its sign) makes agent reliability predictable instead of anecdotal.
why_possibly_novel: MODEL SPECULATION (unverified): pipeline reliability theory is classical for independent stages; measuring the context-coupling correction for LLM-orchestrated visual pipelines may be new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: For a 4-6 step visual pipeline, measure each step's success rate in isolation (clean inputs), then end-to-end success; compute the deviation from the product across depths and pipeline variants; test whether isolating context (fresh sessions per step) restores independence.
main_risk: Defining per-step success in isolation requires clean-input distributions that match deployment marginals; mismatch would bias the product prediction.
community_default_belief: Chain reliability is the product of link reliabilities; make each step good and the pipeline follows.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Links in a chain do not read each other's output narratives; agent steps do, and a slightly wrong narrative poisons every downstream conditional.
fastest_falsification_experiment: One day, single GPU: one 4-step pipeline, step-wise and end-to-end measurement, deviation estimate, fresh-session control. Public data only.

evidence_label.falsifiable_prediction: EXPECTED RESULT (pre-registered threshold; no measured numbers)
evidence_label.prior_work_basis: VERIFIED PRIOR WORK (well-known): independent-stage reliability theory is classical; the coupling-term measurement is MODEL SPECULATION.

one_line_idea: Under mandatory iso-cost accounting — agent loop versus a bigger single model at matched dollars or FLOPs — a substantial share of reported loop gains disappears, exposing the field's default comparison (loop vs same-size single pass) as systematically flattering.
problem: Agent-vision papers compare their loop against the same base model without the loop, burying the fact that the loop spends multiples of the base cost; the fair alternative at that spend — a larger model, more samples of a better model — is rarely priced in.
core_hypothesis: A reproducible iso-cost protocol (fixed accounting rules for tokens, encodes, and tool calls; comparison lines at matched spend) will show that a large fraction of loop advantage is purchased compute rather than architectural insight, while identifying the specific loop mechanisms that survive normalization as genuinely efficient.
falsifiable_prediction: Under iso-FLOP normalization against scaled single-model baselines, average loop advantage shrinks by at least 50% across reproduced open pipelines, with at least one mechanism class (e.g., resolution recovery) surviving normalization. KILL: the claim dies if loop gains shrink by 20% or less under honest normalization (loops are efficient as claimed).
why_important: The comparison standard shapes the whole research direction; if loops are mostly compute repackaged, the community should optimize spend allocation rather than loop machinery — and the surviving mechanisms deserve focused investment.
why_possibly_novel: MODEL SPECULATION (unverified): iso-compute critiques exist for test-time scaling in reasoning; a systematic iso-cost reproduction across open vision-agent pipelines may be new.
