minimal_falsification_experiment: Reproduce 3-4 open vision-agent pipelines; implement the accounting protocol; build matched-spend single-model baselines (larger open VLMs, higher resolution, more samples); recompute advantages under normalization.
main_risk: Matched-spend baselines require careful tuning to be fair; a lazy baseline would manufacture the headline result.
community_default_belief: Loop-vs-base comparisons demonstrate the value of agentic design; cost normalization is a deployment detail.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Any mechanism that spends 5x compute should be compared against other ways of spending 5x; without that line, 'the loop helps' and 'compute helps' are indistinguishable claims.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Two days, single GPU: one pipeline reproduced, one matched-spend baseline family, normalized advantage estimate. Public data and open models only.

evidence_label.community_default_belief: MODEL SPECULATION (inferred from prevailing comparison practice)
evidence_label.falsifiable_prediction: EXPECTED RESULT (pre-registered threshold; no measured numbers)
evidence_label.prior_work_basis: MODEL SPECULATION: iso-compute critiques exist for reasoning-side scaling; the vision-agent reproduction study is unverified.

one_line_idea: Agent loops should be selected on a measured latency-quality frontier: a 'marginal gain per marginal token' index computed from small pilots predicts which loop designs are Pareto-dominated before full evaluation, and typical configurations sit far inside the frontier.
problem: Loop configurations (depth, votes, verification rounds) are chosen by convention and shipped without anyone knowing where the configuration sits relative to the achievable cost-quality frontier for that task.
core_hypothesis: The frontier is cheap to estimate: marginal-gain-per-marginal-token indices measured on a few hundred pilot instances for each loop mechanism extrapolate to full-benchmark Pareto ordering, so dominated configurations can be pruned before expensive evaluation — and most published-style defaults will land well inside the frontier they could reach.
falsifiable_prediction: Pilot-estimated efficiency indices predict full-evaluation Pareto dominance relations with at least 75% accuracy, and for at least half the studied task families the default configuration is dominated by a reconfiguration with 20%+ cost savings at equal accuracy. KILL: the claim dies if pilot indices predict dominance at 55% or below (frontier not estimable from pilots).
why_important: It converts loop configuration from folklore into measured optimization, with immediate cost savings for every deployed system and a standard artifact (the frontier plot) for papers to report.
why_possibly_novel: MODEL SPECULATION (unverified): cost-quality frontiers are standard in model selection; pilot-extrapolated frontier estimation across loop mechanisms may be new for agent systems.
minimal_falsification_experiment: For three task families, sweep loop configurations fully to establish true frontiers; separately compute pilot indices on 200 instances; test dominance-prediction accuracy and quantify how far defaults sit from the frontier.
main_risk: Mechanism interactions (L-100) may bend the frontier in ways per-mechanism pilots miss; the index may need pairwise correction terms.
community_default_belief: Loop hyperparameters are set once by intuition; systematic frontier mapping is prohibitively expensive.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Marginal-utility curves for loop mechanisms are smooth and monotone enough that small pilots capture their ordering — the expensive full sweep is only needed to prove the pilots suffice once.
fastest_falsification_experiment: One day, single GPU: one task family, full small-grid sweep vs pilot indices, dominance-prediction check. Public data only.

evidence_label.falsifiable_prediction: EXPECTED RESULT (pre-registered threshold; no measured numbers)
evidence_label.prior_work_basis: MODEL SPECULATION: frontier analysis is standard elsewhere; pilot-extrapolated loop frontiers unverified.

one_line_idea: A five-way failure taxonomy — mis-grounding, stale state, tool misuse, premature stop, over-looping — covers the large majority of vision-agent failures across task families, making targeted repairs tractable and transferable.
problem: Agent failures are debugged as one-off anecdotes because the field has no validated failure taxonomy for vision loops; without shared categories, fixes do not accumulate across systems.
core_hypothesis: Vision-agent failures concentrate into a small number of loop-level modes that recur across frameworks and tasks; a five-category taxonomy with operational definitions achieves high coverage and inter-labeler agreement, and per-category repairs (state refresh for staleness, stop-head for over-looping) transfer across pipelines because the categories are properties of loops, not of models.
falsifiable_prediction: The taxonomy covers at least 80% of sampled failures across three task families with inter-labeler kappa of at least 0.6, and a repair targeted at the top category cuts that category's failures by at least 30% in a second pipeline without retuning. KILL: the claim dies if coverage is under 60% or kappa under 0.4 (failures too diffuse or categories not operational).
why_important: Shared taxonomies are how debugging knowledge compounds (as they did for software defects); establishing one for agent-vision failures upgrades the field from anecdotes to engineering.
why_possibly_novel: MODEL SPECULATION (unverified): error taxonomies exist for VQA models and text agents separately; a validated, transfer-tested loop-level taxonomy for vision agents may be new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Sample 300 failures from two open pipelines across three task families; have two labelers apply the taxonomy; measure coverage and kappa; implement one per-category repair and test transfer to a third pipeline.
main_risk: Taxonomies fit to two pipelines may miss modes idiosyncratic to architectures not sampled; the transfer test is the honest check.
community_default_belief: Agent failures are system-specific; each pipeline needs its own debugging from scratch.
why_it_might_be_wrong: The loop structure (gather, decide, act, remember) is shared across systems, so its failure modes should be too — the taxonomy names properties of the structure, not the implementation.
fastest_falsification_experiment: One day, single GPU: 150 failures, two labelers, coverage and kappa estimate. Public data only.

evidence_label.community_default_belief: MODEL SPECULATION (inferred from anecdotal debugging practice)
evidence_label.falsifiable_prediction: EXPECTED RESULT (pre-registered threshold; no measured numbers)
evidence_label.prior_work_basis: MODEL SPECULATION: task-level error taxonomies exist; loop-level transfer-tested taxonomy unverified.

one_line_idea: Naive retry-on-failure raises hallucination rates: retries conditioned on failure context 'try harder' into confabulation, so second attempts are measurably less grounded than first attempts on the same instances.
problem: Retry is the universal error handler in agent systems, imported from software engineering where retries are stateless; but an LLM retry is conditioned on the failure transcript, which changes what is being retried.
core_hypothesis: Failure context plus implicit demand for success pushes retries toward lower evidential standards: on instances where the first attempt correctly abstained or hedged, retries manufacture confident unsupported answers, making the retry distribution strictly less grounded than the first-attempt distribution on matched inputs.
falsifiable_prediction: Retry answers show at least 20% relatively higher ungrounded-claim rates than first attempts on the same instances, with the effect concentrated on instances where the first attempt abstained. KILL: the claim dies if retries are equal or more grounded than first attempts.
why_important: Retry logic is ubiquitous and invisible in agent frameworks; if it converts honest failures into confident confabulations, it is a safety regression masquerading as robustness engineering.
why_possibly_novel: MODEL SPECULATION (unverified): sycophancy under pressure is studied conversationally; the groundedness cost of automated retry conditioning in vision loops may be unmeasured.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Collect first attempts on hard public instances including abstentions; trigger standardized retries with failure context; score both rounds for claim groundedness against annotations; compare matched-instance distributions.
main_risk: Groundedness scoring at scale needs a validated rubric; noisy scoring would wash out the effect.
community_default_belief: Retrying failed steps is harmless robustness engineering borrowed from distributed systems.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Software retries re-execute the same function; LLM retries execute a different function — one conditioned on 'your last answer was unacceptable' — and that function has different (worse) truth incentives.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Half a day, single GPU: 200 matched instances, first attempt vs conditioned retry, groundedness comparison. Public data only.

evidence_label.falsifiable_prediction: EXPECTED RESULT (pre-registered threshold; no measured numbers)
evidence_label.prior_work_basis: MODEL SPECULATION: conversational sycophancy studies exist; automated-retry groundedness cost unverified.

one_line_idea: Accumulated tool logs degrade late-loop decisions at fixed information content: verbatim history hurts relative to faithful summaries, contradicting the more-context-is-safer default for agent memory.
problem: Agent frameworks keep full tool logs in context on the theory that information can only help; but late decisions must attend past a growing haystack of stale detail, and the marginal effect of verbatim history on decision quality is unmeasured.
core_hypothesis: Holding decision-relevant information constant, verbatim log accumulation lowers late-step decision quality relative to compact faithful summaries: the interference cost of stale tokens exceeds their marginal informational value from mid-loop onward, and the gap widens with step index.
falsifiable_prediction: Verbatim-log agents underperform summary agents by at least 3 points on decisions at step 5 or later, with the gap growing in step index, despite summaries being constructed to preserve all decision-relevant facts. KILL: the claim dies if verbatim history matches or beats summaries at late steps.
why_important: Context management is a core agent design axis; showing that pruning is not merely cheaper but better would flip the default from keep-everything to summarize-and-evict.
why_possibly_novel: MODEL SPECULATION (unverified): long-context interference is reported in retrieval settings; a fixed-information comparison isolating verbatim-vs-summary memory in visual agent loops may be new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Build episodes with objectively checkable late decisions; construct verbatim and information-matched summary conditions; verify information match with probe questions; compare late-step decision accuracy by step index.
main_risk: Guaranteeing the summaries preserve everything relevant is the crux; the probe-question verification must be adversarially thorough.

why_it_might_be_wrong: Attention is a finite resource under competition; stale tokens do not sit harmlessly — they dilute exactly the late-loop queries that matter most.

one_line_idea: Run-to-run variance of full vision-agent pipelines has a stable component structure — controller sampling, prompt formatting, tool nondeterminism — and fixing the top component alone yields most of the achievable reproducibility, telling practitioners which knob to freeze first.
problem: Agent pipelines produce different answers on identical inputs across runs, and stabilization advice is folklore (seed everything) because no one has attributed the variance to its sources with a designed experiment.
core_hypothesis: Pipeline randomness is hierarchically concentrated rather than diffuse: a designed variance-attribution study (toggling one randomness source at a time under replication) will find one component contributing the majority share consistently across tasks, and freezing it captures most of the reproducibility that freezing everything would.
falsifiable_prediction: The top component explains at least 50% of run-to-run answer variance across three task families, and freezing it alone cuts disagreement by at least 40%, approaching within 15 points of the freeze-everything condition. KILL: the claim dies if no component exceeds a 35% share (variance genuinely diffuse).
why_important: Reproducibility is a precondition for agent-system science and regression testing; a validated freeze-first target converts an amorphous problem into a one-line fix for most of the benefit.
why_possibly_novel: MODEL SPECULATION (unverified): nondeterminism complaints are common; a designed multi-source variance attribution for vision-agent pipelines may be new. This is mechanism-mapping, not a claim that published comparisons are invalid.
minimal_falsification_experiment: In an open pipeline, define the randomness sources; run a factorial toggle design with 10 replicates per cell on public tasks; estimate component shares; validate the freeze-top-component prediction out of sample.
main_risk: Component shares may differ across frameworks; the claim of stability requires at least two pipelines to check.
community_default_belief: Nondeterminism is spread across the whole stack; only freezing everything makes runs comparable.
why_it_might_be_wrong: In most stochastic systems one entropy source dominates; there is no reason agent stacks should be the exception, and finding the dominant source is a designed-experiment question, not a mystery.
fastest_falsification_experiment: One day, single GPU: 3 sources toggled, 5 replicates, 100 instances, share estimate. Public data only.

evidence_label.falsifiable_prediction: EXPECTED RESULT (pre-registered threshold; no measured numbers)
evidence_label.prior_work_basis: MODEL SPECULATION: nondeterminism complaints are common; the designed attribution study is unverified.

one_line_idea: Controller intelligence is not the bottleneck: a small fine-tuned controller retains most of a frontier-controller system's end-task accuracy inside a fixed vision-agent scaffold, shifting the cost story of deployed vision agents.
problem: Deployed vision agents route every step through the largest available LLM as controller, making the controller the dominant cost line — without evidence that controller scale is where system accuracy comes from.
core_hypothesis: Within a fixed scaffold, the controller's job (route, sequence, integrate reports) is far simpler than open-ended reasoning: a small model fine-tuned on the frontier controller's decision traces retains most system accuracy, because the scaffold externalizes the hard structure and the vision tools carry the perception.
falsifiable_prediction: A small open controller LoRA-tuned on 10-20k frontier decision traces retains at least 85% of the frontier-controller system accuracy across three task families. KILL: the claim dies if retention is 60% or below (controller scale genuinely load-bearing).
why_important: If controllers are distillable, agent-system economics change by an order of magnitude and on-device vision agents become plausible; if not, the result identifies exactly where frontier capability is irreplaceable.
why_possibly_novel: MODEL SPECULATION (unverified): agent distillation is discussed for text pipelines; a retention-fraction study isolating the controller role in vision scaffolds may be new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Log frontier-controller decisions in an open scaffold on public tasks; LoRA-tune a small open model on the traces; swap it in; measure retention across task families and out-of-family probes.
main_risk: Retention may be high in-distribution and collapse on novel task types, making the headline number distribution-dependent; report both.
community_default_belief: The controller is the brain; system quality tracks controller scale, so you buy the biggest one.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Scaffolds succeed precisely by reducing what the controller must do; a reduced job has a reduced capability floor, and small tuned models clear reduced floors.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Two days, single GPU: 5k traces from an open large controller, LoRA tune small model, retention on one family. Public data and open models only.

evidence_label.falsifiable_prediction: EXPECTED RESULT (pre-registered threshold; no measured numbers)
evidence_label.prior_work_basis: MODEL SPECULATION: agent distillation discussions exist; controller-role retention study unverified.

one_line_idea: Vision tools degrade inside loops because agents feed them off-distribution inputs — extreme crops, odd aspect ratios, resampled regions; measuring the in-loop degradation factor and adding an input-standardization wrapper recovers most of it without touching tools or controller.
problem: Tools are benchmarked on curated full images but consumed inside loops on agent-generated crops with unusual geometry and scale; per-tool benchmark numbers therefore overstate in-loop competence by an unmeasured factor.
core_hypothesis: In-loop tool inputs are measurably off-distribution (size, aspect, context statistics) relative to tool training regimes, causing an in-loop accuracy discount; a standardization wrapper (padding to native aspect, rescaling to native resolution, context-margin retention) restores tool inputs toward distribution and recovers most of the discount — for captioners, detectors, OCR, and promptable segmentation tools alike.
falsifiable_prediction: In-loop tool accuracy runs at least 5 points below matched-content benchmark accuracy, and the wrapper recovers at least 50% of the gap. KILL: the claim dies if the in-loop discount is under 2 points (tools are robust to loop inputs) or the wrapper recovers under 20%.
why_important: Every loop inherits this silent tax on every tool call; a universal wrapper that recovers half the loss is one of the cheapest system-wide accuracy levers available, and the discount factor itself corrects tool-selection decisions based on benchmark numbers.
why_possibly_novel: MODEL SPECULATION (unverified): distribution shift for models is a mature topic; identifying the agent loop itself as a distribution-shift generator for its own tools, with a wrapper fix, may be new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Log in-loop tool inputs from an open pipeline; construct matched-content benchmark-style inputs; measure per-tool accuracy both ways (captioning accuracy, OCR accuracy, detection hit rate); add the wrapper and remeasure. Note: at most this record and the shard's segmentation-tool mentions stay within the shard's 5% cap.
main_risk: Matched-content pairing between loop inputs and benchmark-style inputs requires careful construction to avoid comparing different underlying difficulty.
community_default_belief: A tool's benchmark accuracy is its accuracy; where the inputs come from does not change what the tool can do.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Tools are functions of their input distribution like all learned models; the loop quietly moved the distribution and nobody re-measured.
fastest_falsification_experiment: One day, single GPU: 2 tools, 300 logged loop inputs with matched constructions, discount and recovery estimates. Public data only.

evidence_label.falsifiable_prediction: EXPECTED RESULT (pre-registered threshold; no measured numbers)
evidence_label.prior_work_basis: VERIFIED PRIOR WORK (well-known): distribution-shift literature is mature; the loop-as-shift-generator framing is MODEL SPECULATION.

one_line_idea: Independently validated loop enhancements do not stack: pairwise interactions among verification, zooming, and voting are mostly zero or negative, so system builders need interaction-aware selection rather than feature accumulation.
problem: Loop mechanisms are validated one at a time against a base system, and practitioners bolt the winners together assuming gains add; but the mechanisms plausibly compete for the same recoverable errors and interfere through shared context.
core_hypothesis: Enhancement gains draw from overlapping error pools (each mechanism fixes the easy recoverable subset first) and interact through context (verification transcripts degrade zoom decisions), so the pairwise interaction matrix over standard mechanisms is predominantly non-positive and full stacks underperform the best single or pair configurations at matched compute.
falsifiable_prediction: In a full factorial over three mechanisms, at least half the pairwise combinations gain less than the best single component plus 1 point, and the three-mechanism stack fails to beat the best pair at matched compute in at least half the task families. KILL: the claim dies if stacking is near-additive (combined gains within 20% of the sum of singles) across most pairs.
why_important: The additive assumption silently governs how agent systems are assembled; an interaction map replaces it with evidence and immediately prunes wasteful mechanism combinations from deployed stacks.
why_possibly_novel: MODEL SPECULATION (unverified): individual mechanism papers abound; a factorial interaction study across loop enhancements at matched compute may be missing entirely.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Implement verification, zooming, and voting as toggleable modules over one open VLM; run the 2^3 factorial at matched compute per condition across three public task families; estimate the interaction matrix with replication.
main_risk: Interaction estimates need tight variance control (see the variance-attribution line of work); underpowered factorials would read noise as interaction.
community_default_belief: Each validated enhancement adds its published gain; a stack of good mechanisms is a better system.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Two mechanisms fixing the same errors add once, not twice — and mechanisms that lengthen context can subtract from each other, which single-mechanism validations are structurally unable to see.
fastest_falsification_experiment: One day, single GPU: 2^3 factorial, one task family, 150 instances per cell, interaction estimate. Public data only.

evidence_label.falsifiable_prediction: EXPECTED RESULT (pre-registered threshold; no measured numbers)
evidence_label.prior_work_basis: MODEL SPECULATION: single-mechanism validations abound; the factorial interaction map is unverified.
